title: Should we take the CLI-first route to a focused feasibility prototype?
body: The common approach would run Codex exec with JSON events and standard Claude Code with structured streaming, behind provider-specific adapters. They can share assignment/result concepts without sharing identical flags. Codex exec is intended for noninteractive runs; we have not established a native interactive tool-approval reply channel. A genuine planning question can instead end a turn, wait in AsmAI for your real answer, and resume afterward. That is different from approving a provider tool request.
recommendation: Choose this CLI-first candidate and create a separate prototype decision ticket. Test real human question/resume, tool denial and approval boundaries, structured completion/failure, interruption, session recovery, subscription-only detection, and fallback before dispatch. Do not certify exact versions or declare the adapter choice final until it passes. If CLI integration cannot preserve required gates, bring back a concrete alternative for your choice; do not use bypass flags or silently switch to app-server/SDK/API billing.
options: Choose CLI-first candidate and create the feasibility ticket
Use Codex app-server instead of exec, with Claude CLI
Continue documentation research before any prototype

title: Where exactly does automatic fallback stop?
body: A worker may have been dispatched but produced no visible output. A leader may be unavailable even though it is not executing a worker assignment. Both cases need a clear boundary.
recommendation: Treat first dispatch to the provider as assignment start. Before dispatch, use the other configured, compatible subscription provider/model if the primary lacks access; record and report it. Once dispatched, pause and ask you before changing providers, even if no output arrived. Use the same rule for leaders: automatic selection before a leader first starts; after it has started, ask before replacing its provider. Keep independent work moving. After you approve a replacement, reconcile effects and preserve grants, context and single ownership; resume with the same provider when access returns remains allowed.
options: Use first dispatch and the same boundary for leaders
Use first confirmed side effect as the boundary
